ratings_why.fun: Three clear ways to grow one vain giant or a lonely court, each card short and readable, and watching Gottfried swell on an empty lek is a real payoff.
ratings_why.distinct: Empty slots as fuel and Proud gaps make a board shape no current tribe asks for, though Duel itself is a familiar Start of Combat hit.

verdict_why: v3 cleared the Champion and Hen clashes; what remains is wording polish and sim questions, not fixes.

points.text: Champion leans on the word Knight but no card says who is one; a line on the tribe like 'every Lekking unit except Hens is a Knight' would settle it at a glance.

Fantail Warden usually sits in the back row, so in reading order its Shield lands after a front-row Champion has already Duelled. 'Start of Combat, before Duels:' would make it do what players expect.
Master of the Cork-Pop is readable but abstract; a short example on the card (Hartmut re-Duels twice per win, up to four times) would show what doubling means.
Refectory Prior's two thresholds plus a tier gate are a lot for a Tier 2 gold card; one threshold would read faster, and the austerity flavour already carries it.

standouts.why: Sir Hartmut, too deaf to hear the retreat, keeps duelling after each win: the bird's whetting turned into a rule you read once.
Sir Gottfried makes the dwindling order the source of power, and his text carries its own example (6 empty slots: x4).
The Chronicler crossing out a name each spring is the seed's best image, played straight as a sacrifice into the Champion.

weakest.why: Fir-Ridge Yearling is a vanilla Duel body; fine tempo but says nothing about display or vanity.
Sprucehold Envoy is a generic Discover card; the cousin chapter's flavour doesn't show in what it does.
Refectory Prior is plain economy with fiddly thresholds.

flags.note: Sir Gottfried at x4 (x7 golden) on a fed Champion is far past the in-fight guide, on purpose; worth the owner's eye.
Herald of the Last Dawn with Ottokar's free first Duel and Cork-Pop could clear a front row before any attack.
Fantail Warden's Shield timing depends on reading order, which players won't see without UI help.
